records.statement: Bitquery says all drained hot wallets carry Binance PoR labels in its address data, including the five XRPL accounts by the article's sequence. This is strong provider-label evidence, but the raw official Binance XRP address export has not been independently retrieved and cross-matched.

Circle's reported 823M USDC freeze occurred in the main Ethereum attacker receiver. It does not establish a freeze of XRP, native XRPL balances or USDC on XRPL, and it does not demonstrate direct XRP price demand.

Bitquery says some stolen USDT was posted to Aave as collateral for a loan paid out in ETH. The amount, Aave deployment/version and exact collateral position are not specified; this is not XRP collateral or evidence of XRP demand.
Bitquery includes Ripple among token issuers that froze assets, but does not identify the exact Ripple-issued token. Do not infer RLUSD, XRP or a particular chain from this report.
The 233.5M XRP receiver balance and no-exchange/no-mixer/no-bridge observation are only as of 06:43 UTC on October 30. No later balance or transaction refresh is included in this addendum.

Bitquery reports no shared address between the XRP/Solana drains and other chain clusters. Their connection to the wider incident is based on timing, transaction construction and Binance's aggregate; this does not prove a single common address cluster or actor identity.
